Note that some provinces have additional holidays that also create long weekends; the list below covers the nationwide ones.

| Date | Holiday | Observed (if applicable) | Long‑Weekend Dates |
|------|---------|--------------------------|--------------------|
| **Jan 1** | New Year’s Day | Observed Jan 2 (Mon) | Jan 1–2 (Sun–Mon) |
| **Feb 20** | Family Day (Ontario, Manitoba, Quebec, Saskatchewan, New Brunswick, PEI, Nova Scotia, NL, Yukon, NWT, Nunavut) | — | Feb 18–20 (Sat–Mon) |
| **Mar 20** | Family Day (BC, Alberta) | — | Mar 18–20 (Sat–Mon) |
| **Apr 7** | Good Friday | — | Apr 7–8 (Fri–Sat) |
| **May 22** | Victoria Day | — | May 20–22 (Sat–Mon) |
| **Jul 1** | Canada Day | Observed Jul 3 (Mon) | Jul 1–3 (Sat–Mon) |
| **Sep 4** | Labour Day | — | Sep 2–4 (Sat–Mon) |
| **Oct 9** | Thanksgiving | — | Oct 7–9 (Sat–Mon) |
| **Nov 10** | Remembrance Day (observed) | Observed Nov 10 (Fri) | Nov 10–11 (Fri–Sat) |
| **Dec 23** | Christmas Day | — | Dec 23–25 (Sat–Mon) |
| **Dec 24** | Boxing Day | — | Dec 24–26 (Sat–Tue) |

These are the official long‑weekend holidays that apply across Canada in 2023. If you need province‑specific holidays (e.g., St. Patrick’s Day in Ontario, St. George’s Day in BC, St. Andrew’s Day in Nova Scotia), let me know and I can add those as well.
